title: Setalcott Powwow Grounds
summary: The Setalcott Corn Festival Pow-Wow brings Native community members and visitors together at Setauket Elementary School for cultural education and celebration. Dates vary by year; attend only during announced public events.
map_geometry_source: Public event location from OpenStreetMap/Nominatim for 134 Main Street / Setauket Elementary School.
listing_image_alt: Setaukett Setalcott Powwow Grounds School5I5A0306 WEB
why_this_matters: Every July, the grounds of Setauket Elementary School transform into a vibrant gathering space for the Setalcott Powwow and Annual Corn Festival, an event established by Chief Theodore Green in 2005. Hosting this public celebration of family history and culture directly within the modern community provides a joyful, irrefutable reminder that the Setalcott people maintain a continuous, living presence on their ancestral lands.
history_content:
Helen “Hart of Morning Star” Sells credited Chief Theodore “Blue Medicine” Green with founding the festival in 2005 to share Native culture and recognize Setalcott continuity.1

The 2017 gathering was announced for July 8–9. A later report documents the July 19–20, 2025 gathering, with storytelling, dancing, music, and vendors. These changing dates show why the event should not be listed as occurring on one fixed day each year.2
preservation_content: The powwow is connected to public event grounds. Surrounding habitation, burial, residential, and private-property places are not identified.
whereintheworld_content: Setauket Elementary School on Main Street in Setauket is the documented public-event venue. This is an operating school: the map is not an invitation to enter its grounds outside announced public events. Check the organizer’s current event notice before visiting.1
